steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: *pant*...*pant*....

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: They're trying to run!

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Not on my watch!

steps.name: Serene Peddler
steps.text: Urgh... I'll cover you, run!

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Interesting, a Perro blocking an attack for a Sarkaz... Neither of you is getting away.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Ezell, you stay put. Don't you even think about––

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: No funny business, I know. The terminal is on, Miss Fiammetta.

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: Trust me, all I care about is ensuring Cecelia's safety.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Change of plans. You can't stay here. Take Cecelia to the Basilica right now.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: It's more dangerous for us to stay in the open like this.

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: Let's go, Cecelia.

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: Huh? Weren't we going to the big statue? This is the wrong way.

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: We're taking a little detour.

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: What's a detour?

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: It means we're going somewhere else right now...

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: The Ecclesia Requietum.

a.text: I planned to ask Miss Fiammetta for a favor after we reached the Basilica.
To have a high-ranking executor look after her, or the Pontifica Cohors to protect her...
And confirm that Cecelia poses no threat to Laterano...
To let Cecelia see her mother Feoria one more time before she's interred.
If Cecelia's father is a Sarkaz... then she should also be a Sarkaz.
And yet she still has a halo...
If Cecelia was nothing more than another 'exception'...
How could a Sarkaz with a halo be allowed to leave the Basilica?
Even if... even if the worst doesn't befall her...
How would she ever be allowed to leave?
Even if this gets me expelled from the Notarial Hall, I have to try.
I must bring Cecelia to the Ecclesia Requietum.
And at least let her say goodbye.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: You can't run.

steps.name: Merry Peddler
steps.text: She's gaining on us...

steps.name: Serene Peddler
steps.text: What do we do? What do we do? We can't shake her.

steps.name: Merry Peddler
steps.text: This is all my fault... That Liberi's not going to let us get away. Run! I'll hold her off!

steps.name: Serene Peddler
steps.text: But...

steps.name: Merry Peddler
steps.text: Hurry!
Stand back.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: An...do...ain...

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: You're not getting away again.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: SHOW YOURSELF RIGHT NOW!

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: I truly cannot understand why His Holiness would adopt such a... hands-off attitude towards the Astray.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: Can you tell me, Mostima, since the two of you are well-acquainted?

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Not gonna talk about that with you.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: That's awfully petty of you.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: I managed to keep him from killing me, only for you to very nearly do me in.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Hard to forget something like that.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: And that's the reason you always wear a hat in front of me? Doesn't it get uncomfortable?

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: I've been a Legata for this long already. It's just a hat.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: And as for you, you should probably let sleeping beasts lie.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: Do you resent me, Mostima?

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Laterano has always needed the Lateran Curia to keep things going, and that's always rubbed some people the wrong way. So I don't really care.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: I think we have a little misunderstanding. That few fallen angels remain in the Church has nothing to do with the Church itself, but rather the Sankta nature of those fallen angels.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: My attitude may be a bit peculiar, but... do you not deem yourself an aberration?

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Considering the way you're talking to me, aren't you afraid I'll become one of those 'regular fallen angels'?

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: If that was a possibility, I wouldn't be 'talking to you that way' in the first place.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Fine. Let's talk business first. When's Fiammetta getting transferred?

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Nothing good's gonna come out of her sticking to me.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: Shouldn't you be asking her instead?

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Brought it up before. No good.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: And you think I'd have a better shot?

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Looks to me like the convenient part of power is you get to ignore what other people want.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: There's a price to be paid for that... So let's hear it. Why do you want Fiammetta transferred?

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: She said she was my escort. Are you guys not curious as to what needs escorting?

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Of course, there are some who think she's a warden or jailer to a fallen angel like me.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: And they don't know the first thing about Fiammetta.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: I'm just the bait she's using to get at Andoian.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: I'm sure she'd be terribly hurt if she heard you say that.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Alright, I'll try saying it another way... the bait is the Lock and Key I'm carrying on my back.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: And? What's wrong with letting Fiammetta do as she pleases? If she can get rid of Andoain or even capture him and bring him back to the Basilica, I'd be very pleased.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: Or are you saying that even the two of you together can't catch Andoain?

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Not necessarily. As long as Andoain is still fixated on the Lock and Key, he can't escape.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: But... let me think.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: What if Andoain has already found another path?

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: What really sucks is I've moved on. Lemuen has moved on. Maybe even Andoain has moved on... But Fiammetta is still trapped in that rainy night eight years ago.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: There's no way I could bring that up with Fiammetta.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: And it's times like these where I start to miss that good old empathy...

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Oh wait, Fiammetta is a Liberi anyway. Wouldn't do me any good.

steps.name: The Pope
steps.text: This conversation sure brings me back.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: What, are you here to share the wisdom of one who has walked that path?

steps.name: The Pope
steps.text: If you'll allow me to exercise my authority as an elder.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: By all means.

steps.name: The Pope
steps.text: Do you remember what you said to me eight years ago?

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: I don't want to ruin the moment we're having, but...

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Sorry, Your Holiness. I can't say that I do.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: It was, 'No... I still have things to do, and people to protect.'

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Velliv's impression of me is making my skin crawl.

steps.name: The Pope
steps.text: You weren't willing to let me choose for you. So why, now, do you need to choose for Fiammetta?

steps.name: The Pope
steps.text: Each must find her own path. She must find it, and then traverse it.

steps.name: The Pope
steps.text: Vel, this is my same answer to you.

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: We're almost there, Cecelia.

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: I'm sorry I'm so slow, Mister Ezell... The sun is about to go behind the mountain.

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: You're doing a great job! Even though we can't use public transit, we're almost off the plate. If I were as strong as Miss Fiammetta, you wouldn't have to work so hard.

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: It's okay! Actually, Mamma took me out once and we went somewhere far, far away from home... just like here.

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: But, won't Miss Fiammetta find out that we sneaked out here?

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: If she's only looking for my terminal's signal... then hopefully that will buy me a little bit of time.

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: The important thing is that we're here.

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: Is this where Mamma went?

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: Cecelia... I've been thinking about how to explain this to you for a long time.

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: Feoria, your mama... is here. But she's also not.

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: I have no way of letting you see your mama again, but at least you'll be able to say goodbye to her here.

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: Mister Ezell... I don't think I get... what you're saying...

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: If she's here, but she's also not, does that mean... she went somewhere else?

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: Where did she go?

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: Let's head in first.

steps.name: Lateran Citizen
steps.text: Before my father passed away, he always hoped there would be nothing but smiles at his funeral. That we'd see no tears. But, I...

steps.name: Warm Prioress
steps.text: If I may, I believe what your esteemed father truly wished was for you not to fall into grief over his passing.

steps.name: Warm Prioress
steps.text: Whether through tears or laughter, if that is your way of sending him off... then I'm sure he will gladly accept your sentiments.

steps.name: Lateran Citizen
steps.text: Thank you... Seniora Prioress...

steps.name: Warm Prioress
steps.text: Allow me to accompany you around the flower fields outside.

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: Mister Ezell, that lady also said that her father 'passed away'...

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: Yes... People who pass away all come here.

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: People who are alive come to send them off... And after that, they carry on the wishes of the person who passed away, and continue on with life.

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: Then what about the people who passed away? What do they do?

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: Maybe... they're watching us from up high in the sky.

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: So we won't be able to see them again because they went into the sky?

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: Cecelia, this is for you.

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: This is... Mamma's guardian gun?

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: My mama and papa were both executors for the Notarial Hall. I didn't see them much when I was little... and it was my nonno who raised me.

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: Nonno really loved his gun, and he'd tell me stories about his younger days every time he polished it.

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: He told me about the battles he fought, his friends, how he met my nonna, and the embarrassing things my papa did as a kid...

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: When I saw my nonno's gun, I would think back to the stories he told me.

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: Later, my nonno passed away. I was only a little older than you are now.

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: An executor from the Notarial Hall came and took away his guardian gun.

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: Just like how I was supposed to take away your mama's gun.
Ezell slowly crouches down and places Feoria's gun in Cecelia's hand.
She lowers her head and looks at her mother's patron firearm.
Ezell gently holds Cecelia's hand.
Warm drops of water fall onto the embossed floral pattern of the patron firearm's grip, collecting into a little pool in the young girl's palms.

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: Mister Ezell... Why am I crying...?

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: I watered the plants in the backyard every week, just like my nonno had taught me. When they blossomed, I was very happy and called for him to come and see.

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: But it was only when I called for him that I realized he wasn't there anymore.

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: I would never see my nonno again, or his gun.

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: Death is the last goodbye you'll ever say to someone.
But, to say goodbye is to overcome death.
For there to be a 'goodbye,' the living must move forward while the dead stay behind.
A 'goodbye' is the longing that the living have for the dead. It is proof that the dead lived.

steps.name: Friar
steps.text: And that is why we must say goodbye.
